transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been avoiding things, more than I want to admit. Anything that reminds me of that old job — office buildings, security talks, even those networking events near work sites — I just find a way not to go.

And if somebody starts asking about the day it happened, I’ll make an excuse and leave. I mean, I used to be the person who handled everything at work, you know? Schedules, people, problems — I could juggle all of it. Now I’m sitting in my car deciding whether a building looks too much like that place. It’s embarrassing.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or on edge when you’re in places or situations that remind you of that job or the event?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I start out telling myself it’s just a building or just some work thing, but if it reminds me of that old job, I’ll find a reason not to go. Office buildings, security talks, those networking events near job sites… I just dodge them.

And if people start asking about that day, I’ll suddenly remember I need to make a phone call or check on something—anything to get out of there. It’s not like me, really. I used to be able to sit through anything at work, even the boring budget meetings. Funny, I still remember this one manager who could talk for forty minutes about copier contracts… but now I can’t even handle walking into certain places without wanting to leave.
Do you find yourself having upsetting thoughts or memories about that day when you're not expecting them, like flashbacks or nightmares?

Yeah… yes, that happens. Not always when I’d expect it either. I can be doing something totally normal, like washing dishes, or I’ll be driving and pass one of those warehouse gates — you know, the kind with the chain link and the little guard booth — and suddenly it’s just… there.

The whole scene comes back really sharp, like my mind drops me right into it. I can hear people panicking, voices raised, and my chest gets tight before I even realize what’s happening. It’s strange because I might have been thinking about groceries or whether I paid the electric bill — my daughter keeps telling me to put everything on autopay, but I don’t like giving companies that much control — and then, bam, I’m back there for a minute.
Since that day, have you noticed that you often feel afraid, guilty, or angry — even when you're not thinking about the event directly?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I’d say it like that exactly. I mean, everybody gets angry or feels bad sometimes, right? Especially when things pile up — bills, family stuff, the grocery store changing where they put everything, which drives me crazy because I know where the coffee should be and then suddenly it’s moved.

But afraid or guilty or angry all the time… I haven’t really noticed it that clearly. Maybe I just don’t pay attention to it unless something brings it up. I can tell when I’m uncomfortable, but naming it is harder, I guess.

Since that day, have you noticed any ongoing changes in how you feel or think about yourself, like feeling distant from others, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or trouble remembering parts of the event?

Yeah… the distant part, I guess. I mean, I still go to things. I’ll show up for family stuff, and if one of the younger people I used to mentor calls, I’ll talk to them. I don’t want people thinking I’ve just disappeared.

But it feels… odd. Like I’m there, sitting in the room, nodding when I’m supposed to nod, and everybody else is together, laughing or talking about the kids or some recipe they saw online — my sister is always sending those videos where they put cream cheese in everything — and I’m just sort of behind glass.

I can see them, I know I should feel part of it, but I’m somewhere else. Not on purpose. It’s just like there’s this pane between me and everyone.
Have you noticed that you feel emotionally numb or detached from your surroundings, even when you’re not thinking about the event?

Yeah… detached is probably the word. I don’t know about “numb” exactly, but detached, yes.

I’ll still go over to my sister’s, or I’ll answer if one of the younger folks I used to mentor needs to talk — I’m not trying to cut everybody off. But sometimes I’m sitting there and everyone’s talking, laughing, passing plates around, and I’m nodding like I’m part of it… and I feel like I’m behind glass.

Like I can see the room, I know I’m there, but I’m not really with them. I’m somewhere else in my head. And then I’ll start thinking about something stupid, like whether I left the porch light on, or how my niece bought these chairs that are so uncomfortable nobody wants to say it… but the main thing is, I don’t feel connected the way I used to.
Have you found that you can't enjoy things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family, even when you're not thinking about that day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still do the things. I’ll put salsa music on while I’m cleaning or cooking — I used to not be able to stand still when that came on, you know? My cousin had this one playlist she swore was better than the radio, and she’d argue with anybody about it.

But now it’s like… the music is playing, and I know it’s something I used to love, but it doesn’t lift me up the same way.

Same with painting. I’ll get the brushes out, move the little jars around, wipe the table down twice because I hate when the paint gets in the grooves… and then I just sit there. Or I paint, but it feels like I’m doing steps, not enjoying it.

And Sunday dinner too. I still cook sometimes — because people expect that, and I know how to do it — but that warm feeling I used to get, having everybody eat and talk and go back for seconds… it just doesn’t come like it used to. I’m there, I’m doing it, but the good part feels kind of out of reach.

Since that day, have you found that you often feel hopeless about the future, or that you’re unable to feel happiness or love for the people you care about, even when you’re not thinking about the event?

Yeah… I don’t know if I’d say I can’t love people. I know I love my family. I know that. Like, if my niece calls, I’m going to answer, even if she’s asking me how long to bake chicken like she hasn’t asked me ten times before.

But the happiness part… that’s different. Things that used to make me feel warm, or light, they just don’t land the same now. I’ll put on salsa music, and before I’d be moving around the kitchen before I even thought about it. Now it’s just music playing while I wash a pot or wipe the counter.

Painting too — I’ll set everything out, and then it feels more like I’m completing a task than enjoying it. Same with Sunday dinner. I still cook, I still want everyone fed, I still care about them… but that good feeling I used to get, watching everyone eat and talk, it’s like it’s just out of reach. It doesn’t come the way it used to.
Have you noticed that you’re less able to feel happy or experience joy in general, even in situations that had nothing to do with that day?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s right. It’s not only when I’m thinking about that day.

Like, salsa music used to lift me right up. I’d be in the kitchen moving before I even realized it, and my sister would laugh because I’d say I was “just cleaning,” but really I was dancing with a broom. Now I put it on and… it’s just sound in the room.

And painting, cooking Sunday dinner — those used to make me feel good. Calm, happy, useful, you know? Now I still do them, because that’s what I do, and because people still have to eat. But it feels like I’m going through the motions. The good feeling just doesn’t come the way it used to.
